entities.summary: Elipandus (717–805) was a Spanish theologian and the archbishop of Toledo from 782. He was condemned by the Catholic Church as an Adoptionist. A student of the prominent theologian Aldrich of Metz, Elipandus was influenced by the teachings of Theodore of Mopsuestia and the writings of the early Church Fathers, including Origen and Gregory of Nazianzus. He sought to reconcile the doctrine of the Incarnation with the pre-existence of Christ, proposing that Christ pre-existed as the Son of God before his incarnation. This theological stance earned him the nickname 'the Adoptionist', and his ideas were deemed heretical by the Church, leading to his condemnation and eventual death by martyrdom. Despite this, Elipandus' teachings continued to influence the development of theology and the understanding of the Incarnation, particularly among the Visigoths. His legacy also highlights the complex and often fraught relationship between the Catholic Church and the early Christian communities of Spain.
